# Drop impact (data analysis & visulaization)

This tutorial demonstrates how to visualize total internal reflection microscopy (TIRM) GIF videos that capture the failure mode of an air film during drop impact. Four evenly spaced frames are displayed from each GIF file. For this tutorial you will need to download and unzip data and keep in the same working directory. More information about the dataset is available in the README file.

from PIL import Image
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the GIF
gif_path = 'mul_1cP_We_3p6_TIRM.gif'
img = Image.open(gif_path)

# Get total number of frames
total_frames = img.n_frames
print(f"Total frames in GIF: {total_frames}")

# Choose 4 frames evenly spaced
frame_indices = [int(i * total_frames / 4) for i in range(4)]

# Plot the selected frames
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(12, 4))
for ax, idx in zip(axes, frame_indices):
    img.seek(idx)
    ax.imshow(img.copy())
    ax.set_title(f'Frame {idx}')
    ax.axis('off')

# Add the GIF file name as the main title
plt.suptitle(gif_path, fontsize=14, y=0.8)  # Adjust y for spacing

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
